report.tagline: An app of very long audio stories told in short daily episodes, where the first episodes are free and you pay small amounts to unlock the rest.
report.simpleSummary: Pocket FM is like a TV soap opera, but for your ears. Its stories, often romance, fantasy or revenge, run for hundreds or even thousands of episodes of 10 to 15 minutes each. The first episodes are free, then you buy coins to unlock the next ones, usually for a few rupees or cents each. It started in Bengaluru for Hindi listeners and now makes about 70% of its money in the US.

overview.whatItDoes: Pocket FM publishes audio series in English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali and other languages. Listeners pay per episode with coins or buy passes, and free listeners can unlock episodes by watching ads. It finds what stories work using data, and now uses its own AI models to write and voice most new content.
howItWorks: Listeners pick a series from a feed of genres like romance, thriller and fantasy.
The first few episodes are free; after that each episode needs coins.
Coins are bought in packs; some episodes unlock free by watching an ad or waiting.
Each episode ends on a cliffhanger to keep people listening.
Writers and narrators earn from hits; Pocket FM says creators earned over ₹300 crore.
In-house AI models write drafts, voice stories and translate them into new languages.
overview.valueProposition: For listeners: endless gripping stories to hear while commuting, cooking or falling asleep, paid in small amounts. For Pocket FM: a pay-per-episode model that earns more per hour than ads or flat subscriptions.

steps.detail: A Facebook or TikTok ad plays a dramatic clip.
Opens the app straight to the show.
Listens to the first 30 or so free episodes.

Unlocks episodes every day and buys more coins.

businessModel.summary: Pocket FM makes most of its money from listeners paying to unlock episodes, about $415 million of its $500 million run rate, with the rest from ads. The US brings in about 70% of revenue because American listeners pay much more per episode than Indian listeners. AI has made content cheap, so most money now goes on marketing to find new listeners.

revenueStreams.detail: Listeners buy coin packs to unlock episodes, the biggest stream.
Daily, weekly or monthly passes for unlimited or bundled episodes in some markets.
Ads to unlock episodes and in-app ads, about $85 million a year.
Selling rights to hit stories for books, comics or video, a smaller stream.

businessModel.pricing: Free episodes, then coins. Coin pack prices vary by country; in the US a single episode often costs well under a dollar, and in India a few rupees. Prices are shown in the app.
costDrivers: Marketing on Meta, Google and TikTok to find listeners
AI computing for writing, voices and translation
App store fees of up to 30%
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a US listener who spends $20 a month on coins. Apple or Google may take up to $6. Writer and narrator payouts and AI costs take another few dollars. The biggest cost is the ad spend to find that listener in the first place, often tens of dollars. If the listener stays and keeps paying for several months, Pocket FM makes a profit. If they leave after the free episodes, it loses the marketing cost. Indian listeners pay much less, so the US funds the business.

howTheyGetUsers: Performance ads on Meta, Google and TikTok
Launching shows in new languages with AI
growth.moat: Pocket FM has years of data on what stories keep listeners paying, plus its own AI models trained on that data. It has a large catalogue of hits. But micro-drama and audio rivals can copy the model, so data and speed are its main edge.

pmLessons: Small payments add up. Pocket FM shows that charging a little per episode can earn more than ads or a flat fee, if each episode ends with a reason to continue.
Follow the money, not the users. Its listeners are mostly Indian, but its revenue is mostly American.
AI can cut content cost about 80 times, but quality and trust must hold, or listeners stop paying.
When growth depends on paid ads, retention decides profit. A listener who leaves after the free episodes is a loss.

interviewQuestions.question: Why does Pocket FM earn about 70% of its money in the US when it started in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare willingness to pay, card and app store payments, price per episode and ad rates in each market. Show revenue per listener, not users, decides where money comes from. Then say what this means for where to invest.

interviewQuestions.question: Users complain about overspending on coins. How would you fix this without killing revenue?
interviewQuestions.hint: Separate healthy heavy users from regretful ones. Propose caps, clear series prices and sleep-safe autoplay. Track refunds and ratings as guardrails, and long-term payer retention as the win.

interviewQuestions.question: AI now makes 99% of new content. What are the risks and how would you manage them?
interviewQuestions.hint: List risks: quality, sameness, listener trust, writer supply, rules on AI labels. Propose quality checks, human review of hits and labels. Measure completion and ratings of AI versus human shows.

interviewQuestions.question: Design the pricing for a new audio series market, such as Brazil.
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare per-episode coins, passes and subscriptions. Consider local payment methods and price levels. Pick one to test first and set conversion, revenue per payer and churn as metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you decide within two weeks if a new show is a hit?
interviewQuestions.hint: Use early signals: day-1 completion, share of listeners reaching the paywall, free-to-paid conversion and repeat unlocks. Compare to past hits and set a threshold for more marketing.
